additional_concerns: Paragraph 10 establishes continuing ultimate responsibility, but does not itself define retained authority, supervision and satisfactory outcomes as a complete conjunctive test. The candidate's proposed test needs an applicable standard and evidence before it can determine substantive fulfillment.

Proper ownership records and operational compatibility are expressly required by s2. Neither accurate vendor records alone nor formal retention of authority establishes fulfillment of the whole responsibility. Conversely, the excerpts do not establish strict liability for every incident or a rule treating missing evidence as substantive failure.
The assessment period, severity thresholds, duration, remediation rules and actual operational facts are absent. No fulfillment verdict is established.

Paragraph 14 places 'upon SFC’s request' immediately before demonstration, supporting continuing confirmation and request-conditioned demonstration to SFC satisfaction. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content; its standalone wording also permits an unresolved broader demonstration reading. Neither reading automatically makes SFC satisfaction the substantive paragraph 10 performance standard.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining an audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Without such requests, those procurement duties are not triggered by these passages; underlying operational and record-keeping responsibilities remain.

The register-address disclosure in s8 is separately request-conditioned and does not determine paragraph 10 fulfillment. The valuation-specific standard in s9 and intermediary-specific standards in s12–s13 cannot automatically become universal Product Provider requirements.
No executable meaning exists for this candidate. Retrieval results establish locations only, and the unsupported structural check establishes no legal or executable fidelity.
